data.name: Jerome
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew name 'Yirmeyahu', which means 'God will raise up' or 'Exalted by God'. Jerome is the name of several figures in Christian history and literature, including the famous scholar and translator of the Latin Vulgate Bible.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name representing faith and devotion to God.
data.numerology_meaning: The number 8 is associated with the concept of balance and harmony. It represents material and financial abundance, as well as the power to manifest one's desires through hard work and determination.

saint_reference.note: a significant saint in Christian tradition, known for his translation of the Bible into Latin

data.cultural_impact: Jerome, being named after the prominent early Christian scholar and translator, is a name that carries the weight of intellectual pursuit and scholarly tradition within the Christian community. The name suggests a deep connection to the Bible and the Christian faith, with a commitment to learning, research, and preservation of sacred texts.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Jerome communicates a deep sense of reverence for God's word and a devotion to dedicating one's life to its study. It is a reminder of the importance of seeking knowledge and understanding of the Scriptures, as well as the attributes of God - exaltedness, power, and presence in one's life. It also resonates with the themes of being raised up or exalted by God, and inspiring others to do the same through one's actions and achievements.

historical_references.reference: Jerome translated the Bible into Latin, producing the Vulgate version which became the standard text for the Western Church for centuries. This work was completed around 405 AD.
historical_references.context: The need for a single, authoritative Latin text of the Bible arose due to the linguistic diversity of the Roman Empire and the desire to standardize Christian doctrine.

historical_references.reference: Jerome is also known for his commentaries and letters, particularly his correspondence with Augustine of Hippo. These writings greatly influenced the development of early Christian theology and the Western Church.
historical_references.context: Jerome's theological insights and his role as a key intermediary in the development of the Western Church's doctrine made him an influential figure in early Christian thought.

modern_usage.modern_context: Jerome is known for his significant contributions to Biblical scholarship, translation work, and literary criticism, particularly in the Latin translation of the Bible known as the Vulgate. In the modern world, Jerome's influence is felt in academia where scholars continue to study his works and methods, in the publishing industry where his translations are still used and referenced, and in the digital humanities where his works are being digitized and analyzed using modern computational tools.

name_in_real_life.story: Elizabeth Jerome, a minister in Athens, Greece, shares that their name Jerome meaning "Exalted by God" has been a constant source of inspiration, guiding them to serve others and live according to Christian values.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Jerome, derived from the Hebrew name "Jiram" meaning "exalted name," symbolizes the proud and elevated identity of a Christian, reflecting the divine nature bestowed upon believers. It encourages the bearer to live up to this holy name, embodying the wisdom and strength of the sainted Jerome, the great translator of the Bible.
